content.thinking:
I should plan the whole scene in one pass without testing: a round sandy base around 2.6m across, a raised central pond, a ring of rocks, palms with curved banded trunks and frond cards, striped cone-shaped tents, and simplified whimsical camels built from capsule bodies, humps, and curved necks.

Then I'll add dunes from squashed spheres, bushes, crates, jars, and a campfire, keeping the floor touching y=0 and scaling everything to a believable diorama size. I'm working out the builder helpers and imports I'll need, making sure not to leave any unused, and sketching the lathe outline for the base and its rim stripe.

Now I'm shaping the dunes as flattened spheres sunk near the base edge, then laying out a small pond as a thin lathe disc with a water-colored material positioned just above the ground layer.

For the pond I'm adding a ring of small dodecahedron stones around the rim, flat lily pads with lotus cone accents, and thin torus ripple rings to suggest water movement. I'm also sketching a palm-tree generator function that builds leaning trunks from swept curves with varying radius along their length.

Still shaping the palm fronds...

Now I'm planning coconuts as brown spheres beneath each crown, with 9 fronds per palm across 4 palms, then moving on to designing the tent shapes using a lathe profile for the cone body.

Placing the door as a thin extruded arch flap on the tent wall's front, positioning it at the right radius and height so it sits flush against the cone's vertical base before the slope begins.

I'll add a thin rug slab with a striped texture in front of the tent using a flat plane with an svg texture, then plan a second pavilion-style tent variant alongside the lathe-based tents of varying sizes.

Writing the pavilion roof lathe...

Now I'm sketching out a camel builder function that positions legs and body using local-to-world coordinate transforms with rotation and scaling, supporting both standing and kneeling poses.

Still planning leg joints, hooves, tail, and saddle details, then working out a transform helper to map local body coordinates into world space with rotation and scaling for positioning the camel's parts correctly.

Designing the neck with gradient color and a whimsical face: big expressive eyes, floppy ears, and a smile. I'll make three camels total, two standing and one kneeling in a resting pose with folded legs, so I'm working out the parameters for body height and leg positions in each stance.

Still placing head features...

For the blanket, I'm draping a striped box over the camel's back using a paint pattern, then adding little hanging sacks on each side as pack bundles for extra charm.

Now I'm thinking through the rest of the scene props: a campfire ring with stones and crossed logs, crates, jars, sacks, clustered bushes, small cacti, lotus flowers and reeds along the pond edge, and maybe a tiny ruined structure in the back with painted pillars and a lintel for atmosphere.

I'm now working out positions for the pond, four palm trees, and tents so they're spaced apart without overlapping, checking distances between each element to avoid collisions.

Settling on pavilion C's position and size, then adjusting camel placements to avoid overlap with palms—repositioning palm1 and spacing out standing camels, a calf, and a resting camel near the tents.

I'm now checking distances between the campfire, tents, pond edge, crates, cacti, and ruins to make sure nothing overlaps, nudging positions like the campfire and tent B slightly to keep everything clear of each other.

For sand texture, I'm writing a custom paint function that layers wind-ripple patterns using sine waves and noise on top of a mottled base color, blending between lighter and darker sand tones.

For the palm trunk, I'm setting up a paint function that creates alternating bark rings based on position along the trunk's path length, and planning to keep all geometry constructors low-poly to stay performant.

I'm defining a ball helper for spheres with position, color, scale, and rotation options, then moving on to texture SVGs: a rug with a border and diamond pattern, a pennant flag using an extruded triangle, and a crate made of brown planks with grain texture and corner bands.

For the water surface I'm applying a mottled teal gradient paint over the lathe geometry. I'm skipping skulls, scorpions, birds, and other extras, instead adding small darkened footprint cylinders scattered along the sand path between camels, and starting a palm function that will add frond details plus clusters of yellow-orange date spheres under the crown.

Writing palm geometry code...

Adding a second layer of darker young fronds, plus small coconut spheres clustered near the crown. For the pond I'm placing a ring of rim stones using scaled dodecahedron geometry around the ellipse edge, and working out how to scale the lathe-generated water surface to match the pond dimensions.

I'm switching the water to a scaled cylinder for the pond surface with mottled coloring, adding a darker wet-sand ring around the rim, and layering lily pads and pink lotus cones on top plus reed clusters near the pond's left edge.

Now I'm writing the tent function, building a lathed outline for the tent shape with painted stripe patterns alternating between two colors based on vertical position.

Beyond the tent body, I'm adding a trim torus ring at the base, a pole with a gold finial and triangular pennant flag on top, and planning the door with an arched extrusion and tie rods.

Now I'm shaping the door opening as a smoothed arch outline, with a dark inner layer and a gold frame extruded slightly outward at the same radius, then adding a rug placed just in front of the entrance.

I'm positioning the rug plane just above the ground, oriented to face forward with the tent's rotation applied. Then I'm adding three guy ropes running from points partway up the cone to pegs staked in the ground at wider radius, each as a thin colored rod with a small ball peg, before moving on to building the pavilion structure.

For the pavilion, I'm setting up four corner posts as thin rods, then shaping the canopy using a lathe geometry with a scalloped outline that's spun around with segmented symmetry and painted in alternating stripes. I'm also adding a thin valance trim as rotated boxes along each edge, and starting on cushions for the interior.

Checking the geometry now—since the canopy uses four segments with a 45-degree spin, it should form a diamond orientation aligned to the posts, so I'm placing the posts at roughly ±0.22 to match the canopy's corner radius, accepting some risk that the rotation might not perfectly align but should be close enough.

Now I'm sketching the ruins: two hexagonal stone pillars with mottled texture, capital blocks, a thin lintel box connecting them, and a third pillar lying broken on its side via a rotated cylinder, skipping hieroglyph decals in favor of simple gold stripe bands. For cacti, I'm building a capsule trunk with bent rod arms and a pink flower ball on top, using a mottled green color, then adding dry shrub clusters of small spheres with tiny flowers before moving on to the campfire.

The campfire gets a dodecagonal ring of six stones, three crossed log rods with lighter-colored ends, and three glowing cone flames, plus a tripod with a sphere kettle, while skipping seating details. For camp clutter, I'm stacking crate boxes near one corner, lathing an amphora jar with a layered outline and painted stripe bands, adding a few more jars nearby, and sacks made from scaled spheres with a small knotted ball on top. I'm deciding to skip precise footprint placement and any extra whimsical sky elements like a floating sun or distant pyramid dune.

Now I'm starting to define the camel-building function, setting up its transform helper based on position, angle, and scale, then building a mottled fur color and a capsule-based body shape with a countershading idea for the belly that I'm still sketching out.

Adding hump and chest spheres...

Now I'm sketching the neck and head using a swept catmull-rom curve, plus a ball helper for sphere placement, a tail rod with a dark tuft, legs, and a blanket box geometry.

I'm positioning the blanket to drape over the hump with angled side panels and painted stripes, plus hanging tassel balls at the corners, and starting on the pack.

Then I'm placing the hanging sacks at the sides of the body with ellipsoid shapes and a connecting rope rod, and working out the eye positions as white balls with black pupils placed outward and forward on the head.

Now I'm positioning the head capsule and verifying the eyes sit correctly on its surface by checking the distance from the central axis, then placing the nostrils and muzzle sphere with a slight z-scale.

Next I'm adding a thin dark mouth rod across the muzzle, dark eyebrow rods above the eyes, spike-shaped ears with base and tip points angled outward-up, a small dark hair tuft between the ears, and a red torus ring around the muzzle for the halter.

Now I'm placing a gold bell under the neck, trying to position it against the neck's front surface near the collar area.

I'm also working out leg geometry—hip, knee, and foot positions offset per side, with hind legs set further back than front legs for a natural stance.

Still working out leg geometry...

I'm settling on a camel height around .66 scale units for the diorama, treating it as a whimsical miniature scene relative to the palm trees. Now I need to write out the full scene code carefully, watching for type correctness on colors and avoiding unused variable errors.

Setting up types and helper functions...

Checking dune placements near the rim—I need to make sure sphere footprints stay inside the base radius so they don't float outside the edge, recalculating distances and radii to keep them contained.

I'm juggling positions for dunes, cactus, palms, and camels, nudging coordinates around to avoid overlap while keeping everything spread naturally across the scene, front to back.

I'll settle on just two dunes and add ruins and a pavilion as background elements, plus a few footprint pairs near the pond, and now move toward actually writing the full scene with a few hundred parts, including flags extruding from the tents.

Writing rug SVG markup...

I'm importing bezier and catmull helpers for paths, then setting up a height-based stripe paint for the jar's lathe surface. Time to finalize and write out the full code.
